title: The unprepared lesson and Bechet's growl at the Belgian drummer
summary: Bechet reacted to an unprepared lesson with 'would you talk to me that way?'. In Belgium he led the band around the stage to growl at a drummer out of time; the interviewer compares a Garland and Kid Ory fight.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I was going to ask, one time you say you had sort of a bad lesson, and what was the remark he made to you? You told me this afternoon something you wouldn't talk to him that way, or what was it?

Oh, yes. I came in. I hadn't prepared a lesson at all, and I thought I could sort of get by with it. Well, not with Sidney. He said, would you talk to me that way? I just let go with some terrible squawks, and that's what he said. Would you talk to me that way?
That reminds me of the other occasion you told me in Belgium once when he didn't like this drummer. You can tell that little story there, too, if you like.

Yeah, the drummer wasn't doing what he should have done, and Sidney, first of all, started stomping one foot on the stage platform to get him in time, and the drummer still didn't get the idea, so Sidney took the entire band, that's the walking band, around to the backside of the stage, which was open. Well, that's where the drummer was, and when Sidney got there, he growled furiously. I think the drummer came, too, eventually.

I was interested, because other New Orleans musicians I know, too, consider music sort of a form of communication, which it really is, and they'll talk. I think that fight between Ed Garland and Ed and Ori, Kid Ori, out in San Francisco, when Garland knocked him off the stand is when Ori said something to him on the trombone, a few dirty words or something, and made Garland mad.
Well, it's a very expressive form of music.
